deltas: Layered strategy/layer contract with EvaluateLayers/PlanStrategy/capability table and honest PipelineVerdict

Three gateway adapters: PCP (strong nonce ownership, RFC 6887 24-byte wire, PREFER_FAILURE, epoch tracking with cross-transaction baseline), NAT-PMP (weak lease ownership, RFC 6886 delete semantics), UPnP IGD (interface-bound SSDP, scoped description, redirect-refusing SOAP, bounded candidate retry, query-then-delete, strict-port enforcement)
direct-v4 and manual-static layers; manual endpoint validation shared by manager and manual.Layer
DefaultRouteSource: gateway strategies map the default-route interface's own (private) IPv4; Assess stays global-only for direct-v4
Node detection (bounded parallel, temp-tuple hygiene, UDP deferred), traversal profile with fingerprint staleness, mapping journal with serialized mechanism-private State

Per-Forward Manager: acquisition composition, same-tuple STUN seam (StunObserveRequest{Server,Bind,Dial}), §3.5 renewal ladder (DEGRADED at 3 failures; LOST at granted-lease expiry safety margin / confirmed reboot / rewritten external endpoint), lifecycle dispatcher off the renewal goroutine with per-callback panic containment, idempotent Release that preserves the journal record on failed gateway deletes
NAT-PMP epoch baseline across transactions (ClientOptions.EpochBaseline/EpochSeen): renewals detect a gateway reboot the way PCP already does, closing the network review's MEDIUM finding
stun.LeaseSource + NewManagerObserver: shared-port same-tuple observation wiring for the manager

netns TCP traversal lab: Manager-driven end-to-end against real miniupnpd 2.3.4 and coturn with independent vantage verification and post-release verification that is gateway-side authoritative (CPE nftables ruleset holds no forward rule for any released port) plus a supplementary vantage closed-port check; keep-mode setup failures now tear the topology down

S7i release hardening: mapper.Delete panics become failed-delete errors; listener cleanup still completes, journal retention remains honest, and idempotent retries return the stable first error; CurrentJournalError provides race-free journal status
S7i signal hardening: EXIT exclusively owns teardown while INT/TERM force nonzero exit; a real netns regression interrupts KEEP=1 only after all namespaces and daemons exist and asserts zero leakage
behavioral_summary: A forward with an explicit-gateway strategy acquires the listener on the default-route interface's own address, maps it through the detected mechanism, optionally observes the same tuple via STUN, journals the mapping with honest ownership and renewal state, renews near 50% of the GRANTED lease, degrades after three consecutive renewal failures, loses only at the expiry safety margin / confirmed reboot / rewritten endpoint, and releases with ownership-strength deletion that leaves the journal record in place whenever the gateway delete failed.

The lab vantage sits inside the lab topology (11.0.0.1); nothing here is public-WAN evidence, and no public-WAN claim is made. The lab CPE WAN address (11.0.0.2) classifies GLOBAL_PUBLIC because 11/8 is not RFC1918 - correct per the frozen rules.

Same-tuple STUN observation through the real NAT is verified at address level (observed address == CPE WAN). Observed-port agreement with the mapping port is daemon-specific (equal for miniupnpd's PCP/NAT-PMP paths, masqueraded for UPnP) and is not asserted.
The renewal ladder's margin/reboot/endpoint-rewrite paths are pinned by unit tests with scripted mappers; no real gateway reboot was exercised in the lab.

Crash window: a successful mapper.Map before journalPut leaves a gateway mapping without a durable record (no intent-record semantics in JournalStore). Declared as P14 recovery input; the journalized State (PCP nonce) is what recovery must rely on afterwards.

Route-change/suspend-resume monitors for live acquisitions are not implemented; profile staleness protects only future strategy selection. Ownership for NotifyRouteChange/NotifyResume is deferred to P13/P14 integration.
JournalStore is satisfied by MemoryJournal in-tree; bbolt durability wiring is the agent composition root's (P13) responsibility.

The host does carry the pre-provisioned antinat-sandbox identity (uid/gid 12001), and with it the full-repo race run is green (s7h-fullrepo-race.log). Pre-existing environmental prerequisite, unrelated to P12.

When no gateway mapper is configured at all, the detection profile carries no explicit-gateway row (the state enum cannot express not-attempted vs failed). Flagged by review; deferred as a detection-profile completeness gap.

JournalRecord.OperationID has no producer and detection-temp mappings are never journaled: the journal covers per-Forward mappings only; detection-temp mappings rely on their bounded 2-minute lease for cleanup. Flagged by review; P14 recovery input.

superseded_handoffs.reason: The quality/security review returned FAIL on one blocking finding (M1): the S7g per-callback dispatch itself lost panic containment - a panicking consumer callback unwound through lifecycleQueue.drain, whose deferred Unlock then ran while the mutex was NOT held, producing an unrecoverable 'fatal error: sync: unlock of unlocked mutex' and killing the process. Verified empirically at d95d06d (s7h-ma16-red.log). Fixed with per-callback recover containment inside drain; the MA16 regression test pins that delivery continues after a panicking callback. The remaining three angles PASSed but all queued findings were disposed in the same S7h batch: network MEDIUM (NAT-PMP reboot detection structurally unreachable) fixed via ClientOptions.EpochBaseline/EpochSeen cross-transaction epoch baseline mirroring the PCP pattern, plus its LOWs compressed here into known_limits where applicable (Suggested External IP omission, one-sided jitter, rollback-only epoch checks, retransmission budget deviations, TransientResult>=128 project rule, unchecked SSDP response source - all conservative-direction deviations, recorded in the review record); PCP L3 (portless Gateway zeroed) fixed; UPnP L1/L2 (SOAP redirect refusal; v1 post-add verification reconciles mangled echoes - tuple-ours entries deleted, foreign entries reported as possibly outliving the call) fixed; lifecycle MEDIUMs (lab keep-mode setup-failure leak; weaker-than-claimed post-release closed-port verification) fixed with the nftables gatewayRuleAbsent assertion; lifecycle LOWs (FINAL_PORT_REWRITTEN compensating delete on caller ctx, detection note folding + dead IGD comparisons, STUN attempt deadline, OnMapping* docs, panicking mapper.Delete consuming releaseOnce) fixed; manager L4/L5/L6/L8/F6/F10 (journal error field, locked CurrentMapping, deterministic journal IDs, EvaluateLayers failure release paths, cancellable renew ctx, rand-failure jitter) fixed.

review_records.outcome: PASS. Wire codecs verified byte-exact against RFC 6887/6886 text; UPnP/SSDP/SOAP controls all present with bounded honest failure modes; all deviations conservative. Findings (ranked): MEDIUM - NAT-PMP reboot detection structurally unreachable (fresh per-transaction clients, no epoch baseline injection; the RFC 6886 §3.6 SSSoE procedure is not implemented either; fail-safe direction, manager's other LOST paths cover); LOW - PCP renew omits Suggested External IP (§11.2.1 SHOULD); NAT-PMP public-address request is 4 bytes vs RFC's 2; UPnP granted lease never learned (Query parses NewLeaseDuration but Map discards it; pacing/margin desynchronize on shortened grants); renewal jitter is one-sided 50-60% while comments say ±10% (inside RFC 6887's 1/2..5/8 band) and no 4s minimum spacing floor; PCP/NAT-PMP epoch checks are rollback-only without forward-drift; NAT-PMP Map does not refuse internal port 0 (doc says always refused); retransmission budgets deviate from RFC SHOULDs (bounded, acknowledged); TransientResult>=128 is a project rule, not RFC §7.4; SSDP response source unchecked (mitigated by LOCATION scope). Disposition: collected for the unified post-review round (fix MEDIUM symmetrically with PCP's pattern or document; compress the conservative LOWs into known_limits).
